commit.message:
docs: add release cycle page (#3550)

Adds `docs/community/release-cycle.mdx`, the release-cycle documentation
required by
[SEP-3398](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/seps/3398-release-cycle-updates)
(Reference Implementation, item 2), and aligns the governance pages that
SEP-3398 changes.

## Release cycle page

- Schedule: six-month releases, eight-month cycles, and the two-month
overlap, with an example timeline (light and dark SVG) of a March and a
September cycle. Release managers publish exact milestone dates and
cutoff times on the roadmap.
- Milestones table with the timing and outcome of each milestone,
followed by separate soft freeze and hard freeze sections with the rules
for changes in each.
- SEP review and inclusion: what the SEP review queue records,
pre-reviews, how release managers order each meeting agenda, a formal
review timeline (light and dark SVG) from the published agenda to the
end of the seven-day vote, and how SEPs that miss soft freeze are
handled.
- SDK deadlines for Tier 1 betas and stable releases, and the critical
fix procedure after hard freeze.
- Details link to the SEP guidelines, SDK tiers, extension lifecycle,
contributor ladder, and the SEP review queue rather than being restated.
- Adds the page to the Roadmap group in the Community tab.

## Governance changes

These are the changes that most need review, because they alter rules on
existing pages to match SEP-3398:

- `docs/community/sep-guidelines.mdx`
- Sponsorship: a SEP can be sponsored by a working group **or by the
Core Maintainer group** (previously working groups only). The workflow
diagram and steps are updated to match.
- Review: the WG Lead or sponsoring Core Maintainer submits an
`in-review` SEP to the SEP review queue. Release managers schedule
reviews within the release cycle's review window and publish the agenda
two weeks before each meeting. This replaces "reviewed at the Core
Maintainer meeting every two weeks".
- Acceptance: a recorded seven-calendar-day vote. Acceptance requires
more than half of the Core Maintainers in favor, rejection requires more
than half against, and a proposal that reaches neither threshold returns
to `draft`.
- The `in-review` status now means "in the SEP review queue or on the
Core Maintainer agenda".
- Voter eligibility and the handling of revisions during a vote are
stated on the page instead of linking to the SEP.
- The introduction no longer cites the SEPs that adopted the process,
and governance amendments link to the new Amendments section in
`governance.mdx` instead of SEP-2085.
- `docs/community/governance.mdx`: adds an **Amendments** section that
states the SEP-2085 amendment procedure on the page, so other pages can
link to it.
- `docs/community/contributor-ladder.mdx`: adds a **Release managers**
section under Maintainer covering self-nomination, selection by more
than half of the Core Maintainers, replacement, the primary/secondary
rotation and the two-month overlap, duties, handoff notes, the
post-release retrospective, escalation, and the access Core Maintainers
provide. Also includes minor punctuation edits in the roles table.
- `docs/development/roadmap.mdx`: adds a **Next Release** section with
the March 30, 2027 target (replacing December 2026), when planning
starts for the following two releases, and how SEP pull requests opened
before the release cycle took effect are handled.
- `MAINTAINERS.md`: adds a **Release Managers** section that lists the
managers per release. For the 2027-03-30 release: David Soria Parra and
Den Delimarsky (primary), Luca Chang (secondary).

## Test plan

Ran locally: Prettier on the changed pages, `npm run
check:docs:js-comments`, and `mint broken-links`. Rendered both timeline
SVGs to check layout. No schema or SEP files are changed.

AI assistance: GitHub Copilot revised the documentation and wrote this
disclosure.

---------

commit.message:
docs: mark Skills support for Claude and Claude Code in the extension matrix (#3588)

Marks Claude (web) and Claude Code as supporting the [Skills over
MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/skills/overview)
extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/skills`) in the extension support
matrix.

Skills over MCP entered public beta in Claude and Claude Code on
2026-11-24: [MCP servers can now ship skills, run tasks, and more with
Claude](https://claude.com/resources/articles/skills-over-mcp-tasks-and-more).
Claude Code requires v2.1.331 or later
([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#use-skills-from-mcp-servers)).

Claude Desktop is left unmarked. The Claude Code docs list Desktop
connectors and Desktop extensions as unsupported.

commit.message:
docs: fix small errors in the 2026-07-28 and draft docs (#3587)

Fixes small errors found in a sweep of the docs, in the 2026-07-28 and
draft versions. The changelog edits are in 2026-07-28 only.

**Please look at these:**

- Caching: the page now says that `notifications/resources/updated` is
the relevant notification for a cached `resources/read` result. The
existing rule only says "a relevant notification". SEP-2549 pairs the
two, but this sentence is new in a released version.
- Dynamic Client Registration: the deprecation notice gives the version,
the PR, and the twelve-month period from the feature lifecycle policy.
- Elicitation: "**MUST** include the following parameters" now says that
form mode requests **MAY** omit `mode`, because `mode` is optional in
the schema.
- Resources: there is a new Resource Template field list, taken from the
schema.
- Kotlin: the client and server guides need JDK 17, because the SDK's
samples require it.

**Specification:**

- Mark optional fields as optional in tools, completion, and resources.
- Use one metadata URL in the Client ID Metadata Document diagram.
- Fix links to extensions and Skills, and the list of utilities on the
index page.
- Say what `includeContext` does, and fix a request ID in the Sampling
diagram.
- Say that the progress example leaves out required `_meta` fields.
- In draft, the Roots, Sampling, and Logging notices refer to the
release of the revision that deprecated them.

**Guides:**

- Link to the matching specification version, not `latest`.
- Use the error messages that the SDKs print, and correct the commands
and jar names.
- Say that clients need a `subscriptions/listen` stream to receive
`notifications/tools/list_changed`.
- Add alt text to the introduction diagram.

Checked locally: formatting, schema, schema pages, examples, and SEP
pages. The Python, TypeScript, and Ruby error messages come from running
the SDKs. For Kotlin, only the SDK source was read. The link check was
not run locally.

commit.message:
docs(community): align IG charters with SEP sponsorship guidelines (#3531)

<!-- claude-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **David Soria Parra** · [Slack
thread](https://ant-mcp-oss.slack.com/archives/C0BDGKP4PC6/p1794253161846999)_

**Before:** The Authorization IG charter said SEP sponsorship remains
with Maintainers and Core Maintainers and that a proposer "finds a
sponsor". The Financial Services IG charter said SEPs move toward the
core specification "with core-maintainer sponsorship". Both predate the
working-group-first SEP process in #3529.

**After:** Both charters say SEP sponsorship follows the [SEP
guidelines](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/community/sep-guidelines).
The Authorization IG charter keeps its single-venue model, including
that the IG does not charter a sub-group per topic and that a separate
working group is the exception. Acceptance stays with Maintainers and
Core Maintainers. Each charter gets a 2026-11-10 Changelog row.

How: Two sentences in `docs/community/interest-groups/auth.mdx` (Out of
Scope, and the problem-pitch paragraph) and one bullet in
`docs/community/interest-groups/financial-services.mdx` now point to the
SEP guidelines, plus a Changelog row in each. `npm run prep` passes.
This complements #3529, which updates the SEP guidelines themselves.
Charter amendments need Core Maintainer approval under [Amending or
retiring a
group](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/community/working-interest-groups#amending-or-retiring-a-group),
so this needs a Core Maintainer review.

This PR was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code).
